## Statement

On a C2 Gibbs chart $G(T,p,n)$ at fixed composition $n$, with $T>0$, $V>0$, finite $C_p>0$, and a valid local inverse between $(T,p,n)$ and $(H,p,n)$, define the **Joule-Thomson coefficient** by

$$\mu_{JT}:=\left(\frac{\partial T}{\partial p}\right)_{H,n}.$$

Then

$$\mu_{JT}=\frac{T(\partial V/\partial T)_{p,n}-V}{C_p}=\frac{V(T\alpha_p-1)}{C_p},$$

where $\alpha_p=V^{-1}(\partial V/\partial T)_{p,n}$ and $C_p=(\partial H/\partial T)_{p,n}$ are the response functions of [[def-td-response-functions]]. This is a local derivative identity. It does not prove that a real throttle is isenthalpic or that a particular substance cools under expansion.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A fixed-composition open C2 chart with valid $(T,p,n)$ and $(H,p,n)$ coordinates, $T,V,C_p>0$, and the potentials defined in [[def-td-legendre-potentials]].

[F1] [[pthm-td-potential-differentials]]: On a valid chart, $dH=T\,ds+V\,dp+\sum_j\mu_j\,dn_j$ and $dG=-s\,dT+V\,dp+\sum_j\mu_j\,dn_j$.

[F2] [[pthm-td-maxwell-relations]]: For the Gibbs chart, $s_p|_{T,n}=-V_T|_{p,n}$.

[F3] [[def-td-response-functions]]: $C_p=H_T|_{p,n}$ and $\alpha_p=V^{-1}V_T|_{p,n}$ on a valid response chart.

[F4] [[def-td-legendre-potentials]]: $H=U+pV$ and $G=H-Ts$ on their local natural-variable charts.

[F5] [[def-td-si-quantities]]: $p$ is in pascals, $V$ in cubic metres, $U,H,G$ in joules, and $T$ in kelvins, with $\mathrm{Pa\,m^3=J}$.

## Proof

1.1 At fixed $n$, write $ds=s_T|_{p,n}\,dT+s_p|_{T,n}\,dp$ in [F1]. The enthalpy $H$ and chart are those of [F4]. Since $C_p=H_T|_{p,n}$ and $dH=T\,ds+V\,dp$, the coefficient of $dT$ gives $C_p=T s_T|_{p,n}$. Therefore $dH=C_p\,dT+(T s_p|_{T,n}+V)\,dp$. [given, F1, F3, F4, algebra]

2.1 Substitute the Maxwell relation [F2] into step 1.1 to obtain $dH=C_p\,dT+(V-T V_T|_{p,n})\,dp$. [F2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Along a curve of constant $H$ and fixed $n$, step 2.1 gives $0=C_p\,dT+(V-T V_T|_{p,n})\,dp$. The assumed $(H,p,n)$ chart and $C_p>0$ therefore give $\mu_{JT}=(T V_T|_{p,n}-V)/C_p$. [given, F3, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 Substitute $V_T|_{p,n}=V\alpha_p$ from [F3] to obtain $\mu_{JT}=V(T\alpha_p-1)/C_p$. Its units are $\mathrm{K\,Pa^{-1}}$ by [F5]. [F3, F5, step 3.1, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

An actual steady insulated throttle has constant upstream/downstream enthalpy only under an additional open-flow energy balance, negligible heat transfer and shaft work, and negligible kinetic and potential energy changes. This theorem is solely the derivative calculation on a specified equilibrium chart.

## Statement

Under the hypotheses of [[pthm-td-finite-jarzynski]], the mean work obeys $\mathbb E_F W\ge\Delta F$. The conclusion concerns the path ensemble only; individual paths may have $W<\Delta F$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A finite-valued work random variable $W$ under the forward path law and $\beta>0$.

[F1] [[pthm-td-finite-jarzynski]]: $\mathbb E_F e^{-\beta W}=e^{-\beta\Delta F}$.

[F2] [[thm-exponential-two-point-convexity]]: $x\mapsto e^x$ is convex on $\mathbb R$.

[F3] [[thm-finite-jensen-inequality]]: for a finite probability vector $(p_j)$ and real values $(x_j)$, $e^{\sum p_jx_j}\le\sum p_je^{x_j}$.

[F4] [[thm-exponential-is-strictly-increasing]]: the exponential is strictly increasing on $\mathbb R$.

## Proof

**Given:** [F1]--[F4].

1.1 Apply finite Jensen to the finitely many forward paths with $x_\omega=-\beta W(\omega)$ and weights $P_F(\omega)$. Then $e^{-\beta\mathbb E_F W}\le\mathbb E_F e^{-\beta W}=e^{-\beta\Delta F}$. [given, F1, F2, F3]

2.1 Strict increase of the exponential yields $-\beta\mathbb E_F W\le-\beta\Delta F$. Since $\beta>0$, multiplying by $-1/\beta$ reverses the order and gives $\mathbb E_F W\ge\Delta F$. [F4, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Let $(X,\Sigma,\mu)$ be a measure space and let $f_n:X\to\mathbb C$ be measurable with $f_n\to f$ almost everywhere. Suppose $g\ge0$ is measurable and $\int g\,d\mu<\infty$, and $|f_n|\le g$ almost everywhere for every $n$. Then $f$ is integrable, $\int f_n\,d\mu\to\int f\,d\mu$, and $\int|f_n-f|\,d\mu\to0$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** As stated in the item.

[F1] [[def-tdmath-measure-integral]]: integrability, signed/complex integrals, and the reference-measure convention are as defined there.

[F2] [[lem-tdmath-fatou]]: for nonnegative measurable functions, the integral of the pointwise liminf is at most the liminf of the integrals.

[F3] [[thm-tdmath-monotone-convergence]]: the nonnegative integral is additive and positively homogeneous.

[A1] The functions are measurable, converge almost everywhere, and are dominated almost everywhere by the nonnegative integrable function $g$.

## Proof

**Given:** A measure space, almost-everywhere convergence, and an integrable dominating function $g\ge0$.

1.1 The exceptional convergence and domination sets have a common measurable null superset $N$, by countable subadditivity: disjointifying $N_1,N_2,\ldots$ into successive differences and applying countable additivity gives $\mu(\bigcup_jN_j)\le\sum_j\mu(N_j)=0$. A nonnegative measurable function supported on $N$ has integral zero, since every simple minorant is supported there. Redefine all $f_n$ and $f$ to be zero on $N$; this preserves measurability and their integrals, and now convergence and domination hold everywhere. Also $|f|\le g$ pointwise, hence $f$ is integrable. [F1, A1]

2.1 First take all functions real. The nonnegative functions $f_n+g$ converge pointwise to $f+g$. Fatou gives $\int(f+g)\le\liminf_n\int(f_n+g)=\int g+\liminf_n\int f_n$, so $\int f\le\liminf_n\int f_n$. Applying Fatou to $g-f_n\ge0$ gives $\int(g-f)\le\liminf_n\int(g-f_n)=\int g-\limsup_n\int f_n$, hence $\limsup_n\int f_n\le\int f$. Additivity of integrable signed integrals follows by writing each as a difference of its positive and negative parts and using [F3]. The inequalities imply convergence of integrals. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1]

3.1 For complex $f_n$, apply step 2.1 separately to their real and imaginary parts, each dominated by $g$; their integral limits combine to $\int f$. To prove $L^1$ convergence, apply Fatou to the nonnegative functions $2g-|f_n-f|$, which converge to $2g$; it gives $2\int g\le2\int g-\limsup_n\int|f_n-f|$, so the latter limsup is zero. Therefore $\int|f_n-f|\to0$ as claimed. [F1, F2, F3, step 2.1] ∎

## Statement

Let $(X,\Sigma,\mu)$ be a measure space, let $E:X\to\mathbb R$ be measurable, and let $J\subset\mathbb R$ be open. Suppose $Z(\beta):=\int e^{-\beta E}\,d\mu$ satisfies $0<Z(\beta)<\infty$ on $J$, and for every compact interval $K\subset J$ there is $G_K\in L^1(\mu)$ with $(1+|E|^2)e^{-\beta E}\le G_K$ pointwise for every $\beta\in K$. Define $p_\beta=e^{-\beta E}/Z(\beta)$, $\langle Y\rangle_\beta:=\int Yp_\beta\,d\mu$ for integrable $Y$, and $\operatorname{Var}_\beta(E):=\int(E-\langle E\rangle_\beta)^2p_\beta\,d\mu$. Then $Z\in C^2(J)$, $Z'=-\int E e^{-\beta E}d\mu$, $Z''=\int E^2e^{-\beta E}d\mu$, and $-\partial_\beta\log Z=\langle E\rangle_\beta$, $\partial_\beta^2\log Z=\operatorname{Var}_\beta(E)$. The reference-relative entropy $-\int p_\beta\log p_\beta\,d\mu$ is finite and equals $\log Z+\beta\langle E\rangle_\beta$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** As stated in the item.

[A1] $(X,\Sigma,\mu)$, $E$, $J$, positivity/finiteness of $Z$, and the local integrable envelope are the hypotheses of this statement.

[F1] [[def-tdmath-measure-integral]]: the reference measure integral, integrability, and signed/complex conventions.

[F2] [[thm-tdmath-dominated-convergence]]: dominated pointwise limits may be passed through the integral.

[F3] [[def-real-exponential-function-and-e]] and [[thm-derivative-of-exponential]]: the exponential is positive and its derivative is itself.

[F4] [[def-natural-logarithm]], [[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]], and [[thm-logarithm-derivative-and-integral]]: logarithms convert positive products to sums, are continuous on positive reals, and differentiate as $1/x$.

[F5] [[cor-mean-value-theorem]]: scalar difference quotients of the exponential are bounded by intermediate derivatives.

[F6] [[thm-chain-rule]]: the derivative of $e^{-\beta E(x)}$ in the parameter $\beta$ is obtained by composition with the exponential.

## Proof

**Given:** A measure space, a measurable real energy $E$, a positive finite partition function, and the compact-interval envelope.

1.1 For $\beta$ in the interior of a compact interval $K\subset J$, the difference quotient of $e^{-\beta E(x)}$ tends pointwise to $-E(x)e^{-\beta E(x)}$. The mean-value theorem [F5] bounds its absolute value, for small $h$, by $|E|e^{-\theta E}$ for an intermediate $\theta\in K$; this is at most $G_K$ because $|E|\le1+|E|^2$. Dominated convergence [F2] therefore gives $Z'=-\int E e^{-\beta E}d\mu$. Applying the same argument to $-E e^{-\beta E}$, dominated by $G_K$, gives $Z''=\int E^2e^{-\beta E}d\mu$; dominated convergence also gives continuity of both derivatives. [A1, F1, F2, F3, F5, F6]

2.1 The density $p_\beta$ is nonnegative and integrates to one. The envelope makes its first and second energy moments finite. Differentiating $\log Z$ using [F4] gives $-Z'/Z=\int E p_\beta d\mu$ and $Z''/Z-(Z'/Z)^2=\int E^2p_\beta d\mu-(\int Ep_\beta d\mu)^2$. The latter is the variance by expanding its defining square. [A1, F1, F3, F4, F6, step 1.1]

3.1 Since $\log p_\beta=-\beta E-\log Z$ almost everywhere and $\int |E|p_\beta d\mu<\infty$, the entropy integrand is absolutely integrable. Substitution and normalization yield $-\int p_\beta\log p_\beta d\mu=\beta\langle E\rangle_\beta+\log Z$. This entropy depends on the chosen reference measure $\mu$. [A1, F1, F3, F4, step 2.1] ∎

## Statement

Let $(X,\Sigma,\mu)$ be a measure space with dimensionless reference measure, let $E:X\to\mathbb R\,\mathrm J$ be measurable, and let $J_\beta\subset(0,\infty)$ be open. Suppose $Z(\beta)=\int_Xe^{-\beta E}\,d\mu$ is positive and finite on $J_\beta$, and for each compact $K\subset J_\beta$ there is an integrable $G_K\ge0$ with $(1+|E|^2)e^{-\beta E}\le G_K$ for every $\beta\in K$. Under the canonical sampling assumption [[post-td-canonical-sampling]], define $p_\beta=e^{-\beta E}/Z$, $\langle E\rangle_\beta=\int E p_\beta\,d\mu$, and $\operatorname{Var}_\beta(E)=\int(E-\langle E\rangle_\beta)^2p_\beta\,d\mu$. Then $Z\in C^2$, $-\partial_\beta\log Z=\langle E\rangle_\beta$, $\partial_\beta^2\log Z=\operatorname{Var}_\beta(E)$, and the relative Gibbs entropy is finite with $S_\beta=-k_{\mathrm B}\int p_\beta\log p_\beta\,d\mu=k_{\mathrm B}(\log Z+\beta\langle E\rangle_\beta)$. Hence $F_{\mathrm{stat}}=-k_{\mathrm B}T\log Z=\langle E\rangle_\beta-TS_\beta$ for $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A dimensionless measure space, a measurable energy, positive finite partition integrals, the canonical density, and the stated local integrable envelope.

[F1] [[def-tdmath-measure-integral]]: measurable nonnegative energies and their nonnegative integrals are interpreted on the specified measure space; signed integrals require absolute integrability.

[F2] [[post-td-canonical-sampling]]: with $0<Z(\beta)<\infty$, the density $p_\beta=e^{-\beta E}/Z$ is the adopted canonical preparation relative to $\mu$.

[L1] [[thm-tdmath-measurable-canonical-identities]] (current batch 11 draft): under the stated $Z$ and compact-interval domination hypotheses, $Z$ is $C^2$, the mean and variance are its log derivatives, and the relative entropy is finite with value $\log Z+\beta\langle E\rangle$. Its full current proof was inspected; its draft status remains conditional.

[F3] [[def-td-si-quantities]]: $E$ and $\langle E\rangle$ are in joules, $T$ is in kelvins, and $k_{\mathrm B}$ is in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, so $\beta$ is in $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$.

[A1] The reference measure is dimensionless, $Z$ is positive finite on the open interval, and $(1+|E|^2)e^{-\beta E}$ has the local integrable envelope stated in the Statement.

## Proof

**Given:** The dimensionless reference measure, the measurable energy, the normalized canonical density, and the local envelope.

1.1 The hypotheses in the Statement match [L1], including positive finite $Z$ and the integrable envelope on each compact parameter interval. The density in [F2] is therefore normalized and has finite first and second energy moments. [F1, F2, F3, L1, A1]

2.1 Applying [L1] yields the $C^2$ partition integral, logarithmic mean and variance identities, and the finite relative entropy formula. Multiplying the dimensionless entropy by $k_{\mathrm B}$ gives $S_\beta=k_{\mathrm B}(\log Z+\beta\langle E\rangle_\beta)$; since $\beta k_{\mathrm B}=1/T$, rearranging gives $F_{\mathrm{stat}}=\langle E\rangle_\beta-TS_\beta=-k_{\mathrm B}T\log Z$. This conclusion is conditional on the draft mathematical supplier. [F2, F3, L1, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume AC. Let $H$ be a self-adjoint quantum Hamiltonian bounded below with a complete discrete energy eigenfamily of finite multiplicity, and let $\rho_0$ be any positive trace-class density operator of trace one. Let $\hbar>0$ be the assigned action constant in $\mathrm{J\,s}$, adopt the unitary dynamics $U_t=e^{-itH/\hbar}$ of [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]], and assume the trace-class Gibbs and local moment conditions of [[pthm-td-general-quantum-canonical-identities]] that supply this discrete eigenfamily. Then, conditional on the current batch-12 draft theorem [[thm-tdmath-discrete-quantum-cesaro-dephasing]], the Cesaro state
$$\bar\rho_\tau:=\frac1{\tau}\int_0^\tau U_t\rho_0U_t^*\,dt$$
converges in trace norm as $\tau\to\infty$ to $\rho_{\mathrm{diag}}=\sum_E P_E\rho_0P_E$, where $P_E$ is the spectral projection onto the full eigenspace of energy $E$. Coherences inside degenerate energy blocks remain. The limit need not be Gibbs, and no pointwise-in-time convergence or thermalization is asserted.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A discrete self-adjoint Hamiltonian with finite-multiplicity energy eigenspaces, a trace-class density $\rho_0$, the declared unitary dynamics, and $\hbar$ in $\mathrm{J\,s}$.

[F1] [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]] and [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]: the declared closed-system state evolves by $\rho(t)=U_t\rho_0U_t^*$ with $U_t=e^{-itH/\hbar}$ and unitary group law.

[F2] [[pthm-td-general-quantum-canonical-identities]]: under the semibounded self-adjoint and trace-class Gibbs hypotheses with the stated local moment envelope, the Gibbs operator has a complete countable energy eigenfamily with finite multiplicity for each energy; this conclusion remains conditional on its current draft mathematical supplier.

[L1] [[thm-tdmath-discrete-quantum-cesaro-dephasing]] (current batch 12 draft): under AC, a complete finite-or-countable orthonormal eigenbasis of a semibounded self-adjoint operator, finite-dimensional energy eigenspaces, $\hbar>0$, and a positive trace-one trace-class density, the trace-norm Cesaro average converges to $\sum_E P_E\rho_0P_E$. The complete current proof was inspected; its Step 1 readiness is missing, so this premise remains conditional.

[A1] AC is assumed through [F2] and [L1]; $\tau>0$ is elapsed time in seconds and every phase $(E_i-E_j)t/\hbar$ is dimensionless.

[A2] $\rho_0$ is positive trace class with trace one, and $\hbar>0$ is the fixed action constant in $\mathrm{J\,s}$.

## Proof

**Given:** The trace-class state, the discrete energy basis, the unitary dynamics, and the current draft trace-norm Cesaro theorem.

1.1 By [F2], the trace-class Gibbs and local moment assumptions supply a complete countable energy eigenbasis with finite-dimensional eigenspaces; [A1] supplies AC and [A2] supplies the positive trace-one initial density and action-unit convention. Together with the semibounded self-adjoint Hamiltonian in the Statement, these are the hypotheses of [L1], and [F1] specifies the same unitary orbit. [F1, F2, L1, A1, A2]

2.1 Apply the current draft result [L1] to the matched inputs in step 1.1. It yields $\bar\rho_\tau\to\sum_E P_E\rho_0P_E$ in trace norm with the entire degenerate blocks retained. The limit depends on $\rho_0$, so no Gibbs or pointwise-time conclusion follows. This use remains conditional until [L1] has current Step 1 readiness. [F1, F2, L1, step 1.1] ∎

## Statement

Fix a closed macroscopic system with composition fixed and two admitted equilibrium endpoints. In the fixed-volume model, couple it only to an ideal thermal reservoir at constant $T_0>0$. In the fixed-pressure model, also couple it to an ideal pressure store at constant $p_0>0$. Define the constrained potentials

$$F_{T_0}(x):=U(x)-T_0S(x),\qquad G_{T_0,p_0}(x):=U(x)+p_0V(x)-T_0S(x).$$

Assume the ideal-reservoir bookkeeping specified in [A1]–[A3] of Facts & Assumptions and the adopted isolated-compound second law [[post-td-macroscopic-second-law]]. Then along every admitted spontaneous endpoint change at fixed volume, $F_{T_0}$ does not increase; at fixed pressure, $G_{T_0,p_0}$ does not increase. If an endpoint is an attained global entropy maximum on the same feasible set, the corresponding constrained potential attains a global minimum there. If the system endpoint is on its $T=T_0$ or $(T,p)=(T_0,p_0)$ natural-variable chart, these constrained functions agree with the Helmholtz or Gibbs potentials of [[def-td-legendre-potentials]].

The statement is conditional on the ideal bath/load model and is not a claim that every physical process has such a reservoir or reaches the minimum.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A fixed composition, an explicit feasible endpoint set for a closed system plus its named reservoirs, equilibrium endpoints, fixed excluded kinetic and external-field energy changes, and the following ideal reservoir model. Energies are in joules, entropy in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, $T_0$ in kelvins, $V$ in $\mathrm{m^3}$, and $p_0$ in pascals.

[A1] Ideal thermal reservoir: its energy $E_R$ ranges in an open interval and its entropy is $S_R(E_R)=S_{R,0}+E_R/T_0$ there. Heat $Q$ positive into the system changes its energy by $\Delta E_R=-Q$, so $\Delta S_R=-Q/T_0$.

[A2] Ideal pressure store: at fixed external pressure $p_0$, its stored energy changes by $p_0\Delta V$ when the system volume changes by $\Delta V$; the only system work is $W_{\mathrm{on}}=-p_0\Delta V$. The store's entropy is constant. At fixed volume this store is absent. No other work coordinate or matter transfer is admitted.

[A3] The system and bath, with the pressure store when present, form an isolated compound with fixed total energy. In the fixed-volume case $\Delta U+\Delta E_R=0$; in the fixed-pressure case $\Delta U+\Delta E_R+p_0\Delta V=0$. These are explicit ideal-environment constraints; they do not follow from units.

[F1] [[post-td-first-law-energy]]: For admitted closed core-process records, $\Delta U=Q+W_{\mathrm{on}}$ with heat positive into the system and work positive on it, under fixed composition and zero excluded-energy endpoint changes.

[F2] [[post-td-macroscopic-second-law]]: For the admitted isolated compound with its named auxiliaries and equilibrium endpoints, $\Delta S_{\mathrm{tot}}\ge0$.

[F3] [[post-td-entropy-maximum]]: Stable equilibrium is an attained global maximum of the sum of constituent entropies on the explicitly declared feasible set; uniqueness is not assumed.

[F4] [[def-td-legendre-potentials]]: The local Helmholtz and Gibbs potentials are $F=U-TS$ and $G=U-TS+pV$ on their valid natural-variable charts.

[F5] [[def-td-si-quantities]]: $U$, $Q$, and work transfers are in joules, $T$ in kelvins, $S$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, $p$ in pascals, and $V$ in $\mathrm{m^3}$, with $\mathrm{Pa\,m^3=J}$.

## Proof

1.1 In the fixed-volume case, the first-law balance [F1] has $W_{\mathrm{on}}=0$ by [A2], so $\Delta U=Q$. The bath relation [A1] gives $\Delta S_{\mathrm{tot}}=\Delta S-Q/T_0$. By [F2], $\Delta S_{\mathrm{tot}}\ge0$, and therefore $\Delta F_{T_0}=Q-T_0\Delta S=-T_0\Delta S_{\mathrm{tot}}\le0$. [given, A1, A2, F1, F2, F5, algebra]

1.2 In the fixed-pressure case, [A2] and [F1] give $\Delta U=Q-p_0\Delta V$, while [A1] gives $\Delta S_{\mathrm{tot}}=\Delta S-Q/T_0$. Hence $\Delta G_{T_0,p_0}=\Delta U+p_0\Delta V-T_0\Delta S=Q-T_0\Delta S=-T_0\Delta S_{\mathrm{tot}}\le0$. [given, A1, A2, F1, F2, F5, algebra]

1.3 For fixed volume, [A1] and [A3] express total entropy on the feasible set as $S_{\mathrm{tot}}=\mathrm{constant}-F_{T_0}/T_0$. Since $T_0>0$, maximizing total entropy is equivalent to minimizing $F_{T_0}$; on the natural-variable chart the function is the Helmholtz potential by [F4]. [A1, A3, F3, F4, algebra]

2.1 For fixed pressure, [A1]–[A3] express total entropy as $S_{\mathrm{tot}}=\mathrm{constant}-G_{T_0,p_0}/T_0$. Again $T_0>0$, so every attained global entropy maximizer on that feasible set is a global minimizer of $G_{T_0,p_0}$; on the natural-variable chart it is the Gibbs potential by [F4]. Neither equivalence implies uniqueness or attainment beyond [F3]. [A1, A2, A3, F3, F4, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

The assumptions define ideal reservoirs, not measured reservoirs. A finite bath generally has varying temperature and does not satisfy [A1] exactly. The result does not cover an open flowing control volume or other generalized work coordinates.

## Statement

Adopt exactly the state, observable, autonomous-dynamics and canonical-ensemble assumptions, readings, finite-dimensional sector class, and normalized canonical preparation of [[pthm-nrqm-many-body-unitary-evolution-preserves-entropy]]. The sector $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ and its self-adjoint energy operator $H_N^\sigma$ are those of [[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]]. Model time $t$ is in seconds, $H_N^\sigma$ is in joules, and $\hbar=h/(2\pi)$ is the reduced Planck constant in $\mathrm{J\,s}$, as in [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. The evolution definition [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] gives $U(t)=\exp(-itH_N^\sigma/\hbar)$ and $\rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^*$. Both the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice are assumed ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Define $S_{\mathrm{vN}}(\rho)=k_{\mathrm B}s(\rho)$ as in [[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]]. Then, for every declared sector preparation $\rho(0)$ and every $t\in\mathbb R$:

1. $S_{\mathrm{vN}}(\rho(t))=S_{\mathrm{vN}}(\rho(0))$;
2. the adopted canonical preparation is stationary; and
3. a preparation different from the canonical one is never mapped to it by this unitary flow.

These are statements about the exact closed finite-sector model. They do not identify $S_{\mathrm{vN}}$ with the macroscopic equilibrium entropy $S_c$ of [[def-td-macro-versus-micro-entropy-claim]], derive the canonical preparation, or establish bath relaxation or thermalization.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The complete model assumptions and conclusions (a)–(d) of the published finite-sector supplier, together with its Countable Choice and Choice assumptions; use the definition $S_{\mathrm{vN}}=k_{\mathrm B}s$ and the entropy-domain distinction stated below.

[F1] [[pthm-nrqm-many-body-unitary-evolution-preserves-entropy]]: under the stated finite-dimensional model and postulates, its clauses (a)–(c) prove dimensionless entropy conservation, canonical stationarity, and nonproduction of the canonical preparation from any distinct preparation.

[F2] [[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]]: in the declared finite-dimensional sector, $S_{\mathrm{vN}}(\rho)=k_{\mathrm B}s(\rho)$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$.

[F3] [[def-td-macro-versus-micro-entropy-claim]]: $S_c$ is a function on the equilibrium macrostate domain $D_c$, whereas $S_{\mathrm{vN}}$ is a function on finite-sector density operators; no identification is adopted without an additional bridge.

[F4] [[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]]: the declared nonzero sector has a self-adjoint energy operator $H_N^\sigma$ assigned as its energy observable.

[F5] [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]: model time is in seconds, energy is in joules, and $\hbar=h/(2\pi)$ is in $\mathrm{J\,s}$.

[F6] [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]: the closed-model state evolves by $\rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^*$ with $U(t)=\exp(-itH_N^\sigma/\hbar)$.

[F7] [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]: $U$ is a strongly continuous unitary group with $U(t)^*=U(t)^{-1}=U(-t)$.

[F8] [[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]]: the supplier defines no entropy for its infinite-dimensional spatial sectors.

[A1] [[def-countable-choice]] and [[def-axiom-of-choice]]: assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice, exactly as the published supplier does.

## Proof

1.1 Under the finite-sector model [F4], units and time convention [F5], flow [F6], and both choice assumptions [A1], clause (a) of [F1] gives $s(\rho(t))=s(\rho(0))$ for every declared preparation and every real $t$. Multiplying by the fixed $k_{\mathrm B}$ and using [F2] yields $S_{\mathrm{vN}}(\rho(t))=S_{\mathrm{vN}}(\rho(0))$. This proves conclusion 1. [F1, F2, F4, F5, F6, A1, algebra]

1.2 Clause (b) of [F1] gives conclusion 2 under the same model and choice assumptions. The canonical preparation is an adopted premise of [F1]; its stationarity does not derive that preparation or a relaxation process. [F1, F4, F5, F6, A1]

2.1 If $\rho(t)=\rho_\beta$ for some $t$, then applying $U(t)^*$ on the left and $U(t)$ on the right, using [F7], gives $\rho(0)=U(t)^*\rho_\beta U(t)$. Stationarity in step 1.2 at time $-t$ makes the right-hand side $\rho_\beta$. Thus $\rho(0)\ne\rho_\beta$ implies $\rho(t)\ne\rho_\beta$ for every real $t$, which is conclusion 3. By [F3] the invariant in step 1.1 is defined on density operators, while the macroscopic entropy is defined on equilibrium macrostates; [F8] also keeps the von Neumann entropy restricted to finite-dimensional sectors. None of the premises identifies those domains or supplies a bath or macroscopic relaxation law, so no monotonicity claim for $S_c$, bath relaxation, or thermalization follows. [F3, F7, F8, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume the calibrated entropy family of [[thm-tdmath-arbitrary-family-calibration]], the cross-type accessibility axioms A1–A6 of [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]], and the decorated cost $F$ of [[def-tdmath-decorated-chain-costs]]. For every pair of types $\Gamma,\Gamma'$ and states $x\in X_\Gamma$, $y\in X_{\Gamma'}$,

$$x\prec y\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \sigma_\Gamma(x)+F(\Gamma,\Gamma')\le \sigma_{\Gamma'}(y).$$

The infimum defining $F$ need not be attained. If $F=+\infty$, the right side is false; if $F=-\infty$, the right side is true.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The complete additive extensive entropy on every finite type, the finite-chain cost, and A1–A6 including stability.

[A1] [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]]: consistency permits running accessible edges with common spectators; stability removes fixed positive spectators whose common scale tends to zero.

[F1] [[thm-tdmath-arbitrary-family-calibration]]: every type and finite separated product has a finite real additive extensive entropy representing same-composition comparisons; its Statement fixes a strict meter pair $z_0\prec\prec z_1$.

[F2] [[def-tdmath-decorated-chain-costs]]: $F$ is the infimum of the real costs of finite chains with an arbitrary common catalyst.

[F3] [[lem-tdmath-decorated-cost-algebra]]: every actual decorated-chain witness has a finite real additive cost, and costs have no negative closed cycles.

[F4] [[lem-tdmath-forward-spectator-cancellation]]: common finite compound spectators can be cancelled under A1–A6.

## Proof

1.1 If $x\prec y$, the one-edge witness with an identity catalyst has cost $\sigma_{\Gamma'}(y)-\sigma_\Gamma(x)$. Hence $F(\Gamma,\Gamma')\le\sigma_{\Gamma'}(y)-\sigma_\Gamma(x)$, which is the forward inequality, including the case $F=+\infty$ where no such transition can exist. [F1, F2]

1.2 Conversely assume the displayed entropy inequality. It is impossible when $F=+\infty$. For each integer $n\ge1$, choose a decorated witness of real cost $c_n\le\Delta\sigma+h/n$, where $\Delta\sigma=\sigma_{\Gamma'}(y)-\sigma_\Gamma(x)$ and $h=\sigma(z_1)-\sigma(z_0)>0$ is the entropy gap of a fixed strict meter pair from [F1]. Such witnesses exist from the definition of infimum, also if $F=-\infty$. Write their types as $T_0=\Gamma\times C,T_1,\ldots,T_N=\Gamma'\times C$, their edges as $a_k\prec b_{k+1}$, and their endpoints as $a_0=(\widetilde x,c_0)$, $b_N=(\widetilde y,d_0)$. [F1, F2, F3, choose]

2.1 Put $\delta_n=1/n$. In one finite compound type form
$L_n=(x,b_N,b_1,\ldots,b_{N-1},\delta_n z_0),\qquad R_n=(a_0,y,a_1,\ldots,a_{N-1},\delta_n z_1).$
These have the same composition: both contain $\Gamma$, $\Gamma'$, the catalyst $C$, every intermediate type $T_1,\ldots,T_{N-1}$, and one scaled meter state, up to reassociation and permutation. Additivity of $\sigma$ and the definition of chain cost give
$\sigma(R_n)-\sigma(L_n)=\Delta\sigma-c_n+\delta_n h\ge0.$
Thus the same-composition entropy representation [F1] gives $L_n\prec R_n$. [A1, F1, F3, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 Starting from $R_n$, use consistency on $a_0\prec b_1$ with $y,\delta_nz_1,a_1,\ldots,a_{N-1}$ as spectators. The result contains $b_1$ in place of $a_0$. Next use $a_1\prec b_2$ with $y,\delta_nz_1,b_1,a_2,\ldots,a_{N-1}$ as spectators, and continue in order. At stage $k$, the current compound contains $a_k$, the earlier outputs $b_1,\ldots,b_k$, all later inputs $a_{k+1},\ldots,a_{N-1}$, and the unchanged $y,\delta_nz_1$. After the last edge, transitivity gives $R_n\prec R'_n$, where $R'_n=(b_1,\ldots,b_N,y,\delta_nz_1)$. Compose this with $L_n\prec R_n$ from step 2.1. The compounds $L_n$ and $R'_n$ share the finite spectator $b_1+\cdots+b_N$; cancel it by [F4]. The result is $x+\delta_nz_0\prec y+\delta_nz_1$ for every $n$. [A1, F4, step 2.1]

4.1 Since $\delta_n\downarrow0$, stability in [A1] with bases $x,y$ and fixed positive spectators $z_0,z_1$ yields $x\prec y$. This proves the reverse implication without assuming that any infimum is attained. [A1, step 3.1] ∎

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $F$ be the decorated cost of [[def-tdmath-decorated-chain-costs]], and assume the **no-sinks condition**

$$F(\Gamma,\Gamma')<+\infty\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad F(\Gamma',\Gamma)<+\infty$$

for every type pair. Let $V_F$ be the real difference space of [[def-tdmath-cost-offset-difference-space]]. Then there is an additive extensive offset $B:\mathcal G\to\mathbb R$ such that

$$-F(\Gamma',\Gamma)\le B(\Gamma)-B(\Gamma')\le F(\Gamma,\Gamma').$$

If every admitted cross-type transition $x\prec y$ from $\Gamma$ to $\Gamma'$ satisfies the calibrated cost inequality of [[thm-tdmath-unattained-cost-entropy-inference]], then $\sigma_\Gamma(x)+B(\Gamma)$ is nondecreasing across every such transition. Only this weak inequality is asserted; no-gap equalities and strict extensions are not concluded.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The no-sinks condition, A1–A6 for cross-type transitions, the finite-chain costs, and the Axiom of Choice.

[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]]: adopt AC for the Hahn–Banach dominated-extension and basis-extension steps in the vector-space supplier.

[F1] [[def-tdmath-cost-offset-difference-space]] and [[lem-tdmath-cost-offset-difference-space-well-defined]]: $V_F$ is a real vector space of formal type differences, with composition additive and positive scaling homogeneous.

[F2] [[lem-tdmath-decorated-cost-algebra]]: $F(\Gamma,\Gamma)=0$, $F$ is translation-invariant, positively homogeneous and subadditive, finite reverse witnesses bound forward costs, and costs have no negative cycles.

[F3] [[thm-tdmath-infinite-no-sinks-sandwich]]: under AC, a sublinear $p:V\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$ with $p(0)=0$ and symmetric finite domain admits a linear $L$ with $-p(-v)\le L(v)\le p(v)$.

[F4] [[thm-tdmath-unattained-cost-entropy-inference]]: every admitted transition $x\prec y$ satisfies $\sigma_{\Gamma'}(y)-\sigma_\Gamma(x)\ge F(\Gamma,\Gamma')$.

## Proof

**Given:** [A1], [F1]–[F4], and the no-sinks condition.

1.1 If $F(\Gamma,\Gamma')<+\infty$, no-sinks gives a finite reverse witness of some real cost $c$. Concatenating it with any forward witness makes a closed chain, so [F2] gives forward cost at least $-c$. Thus $F(\Gamma,\Gamma')>-\infty$ whenever it is finite; all cost values are in $\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$. [A1, F2, given]

2.1 For a pair class $v=[\Gamma,\Gamma']\in V_F$, define $p(v):=F(\Gamma,\Gamma')$. Suppose $(\Gamma,\Gamma')\equiv(\Lambda,\Lambda')$ via $C$, so $P=\Gamma\times\Lambda'\times C\approx_0 Q=\Lambda\times\Gamma'\times C$. Put $D=\Gamma'\times\Lambda'\times C$. Since $P\approx_0 Q$, the triangle inequality gives $F(P,D)\le F(Q,D)$ and $F(Q,D)\le F(P,D)$; the costs have no $-\infty$ by step 1.1, so these inequalities imply equality. Catalyst invariance from [F2] gives $F(P,D)=F(\Gamma,\Gamma')$ and $F(Q,D)=F(\Lambda,\Lambda')$. Therefore $p$ is independent of the pair representative. [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 The identity $F(\Gamma,\Gamma)=0$ gives $p(0)=0$. Homogeneity of $F$ gives $p(tv)=tp(v)$ for $t>0$, and its product subadditivity gives $p(v+w)\le p(v)+p(w)$. The no-sinks condition says $p(v)<+\infty$ exactly when $p(-v)<+\infty$. By step 1.1, $p$ has no $-\infty$ value. [F1, F2, given, step 1.1]

3.1 Apply [F3] to $V_F$ and $p$. It gives a real-linear $L:V_F\to\mathbb R$ with $-p(-v)\le L(v)\le p(v)$ for all $v$. Put $B(\Gamma)=L([\Gamma,1])$, where $1$ is the empty unit type. Since $[\Gamma\times\Gamma',1]=[\Gamma,1]+[\Gamma',1]$, $B$ is additive. Since $[t\Gamma,1]=t[\Gamma,1]$ (the unit type satisfies $t1=1$), $B(t\Gamma)=tB(\Gamma)$ for $t>0$. Also $[\Gamma,\Gamma']=[\Gamma,1]-[\Gamma',1]$, so applying the sandwich to this pair gives the displayed two-sided cost bound. [A1, F1, F3, step 2.2, algebra]

4.1 For an admitted transition, [F4] gives $\sigma_{\Gamma'}(y)-\sigma_\Gamma(x)\ge F(\Gamma,\Gamma')$, while step 3.1 gives $B(\Gamma)-B(\Gamma')\le F(\Gamma,\Gamma')$. Subtracting the latter from the former yields
$[\sigma_{\Gamma'}(y)+B(\Gamma')]-[\sigma_\Gamma(x)+B(\Gamma)]\ge0.$
Thus the offset entropy is nondecreasing across every admitted transition. [F4, step 3.1, algebra] ∎
## Remarks

The no-sinks condition is an explicit hypothesis about cross-type reachability. AC is used by [[thm-tdmath-infinite-no-sinks-sandwich]] and is carried here. The result does not assert a no-gap condition, a unique offset, or an exact entropy principle for all transitions.

## Statement

Let $\mathcal G\ne\varnothing$ be a finite-factor-closed network of [[def-td-cross-type-reaction-network]]. Assume the contact hypotheses of [[pthm-td-entropy-under-product-comparison]] provide a finite real baseline entropy $\sigma_\Gamma$ on each type. Also assume that network satisfies A1–A6, its exact decorated-chain cost $F$ has the no-sinks property defined there, and the Axiom of Choice. Then there is a real offset $B(\Gamma)$ for each type, additive under finite composition and extensive under every positive scaling, such that the corrected entropy

$$S_\Gamma(x):=\sigma_\Gamma(x)+B(\Gamma)$$

is nondecreasing across every admitted channel transition: if $(\Gamma,x)\mathcal R(\Gamma',y)$, then $S_\Gamma(x)\le S_{\Gamma'}(y)$. The conclusion is weak monotonicity only. It does not assert a no-gap identity, uniqueness of $B$, strict increase, or a global entropy principle for networks that fail the stated hypotheses.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A finite baseline entropy per type, finite-factor closure, A1–A6 on the cross-type relation, the decorated-chain definition, no-sinks, and Choice.

[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]]: the infinite-dimensional dominated-extension supplier adopts Choice.

[F1] [[pthm-td-entropy-under-product-comparison]]: under the contact branch, $\sigma_\Gamma$ is finite, additive and extensive on each fixed-composition finite product and represents its equal-composition comparison.

[F2] [[def-td-cross-type-reaction-network]]: the admitted transitions have the declared edge costs, the finite decorated-chain cost $F$, cross-type A1–A6, and the no-sinks condition.

[F3] [[thm-tdmath-unattained-cost-entropy-inference]]: for the baseline entropies and exact finite-chain cost, each admitted transition satisfies $\sigma_{\Gamma'}(y)-\sigma_\Gamma(x)\ge F(\Gamma,\Gamma')$; the proof covers unattained infima.

[F4] [[thm-tdmath-splitting-cost-quotient]]: under Choice, A1–A6, the same cost $F$, and no-sinks, there is an additive extensive type offset $B$ with $B(\Gamma)-B(\Gamma')\le F(\Gamma,\Gamma')$, and the theorem states the resulting weak monotonicity whenever [F3] holds.

## Proof
**Given:** [A1] and [F1]–[F4].

1.1 Fix an admitted transition $(\Gamma,x)\mathcal R(\Gamma',y)$. [F1] supplies finite baseline state values on both endpoint types, and [F2] identifies the decorated-chain cost convention used for this pair. Use the composition-preserving type-weighted representation from [F1]'s construction: interpret each encoded coefficient by its amount divided by the positive type weight, keeping the raw scaled and joined tags distinct. The network compares equal formal masses, and this interpretation preserves its admitted endpoint relation and each finite baseline entropy sum; hence each physical finite-chain witness and its coefficient-map image have the same real edge costs. Reversible regrouping of factors uses the adopted reversible-splitting axiom in [F2], so it changes neither the represented endpoints nor their baseline values. The cost $F$ used by [F3] is therefore this exact witness infimum, not one inferred from coordinate equality. Applying [F3] to this exact transition gives $$ \sigma_{\Gamma'}(y)-\sigma_\Gamma(x)\ge F(\Gamma,\Gamma'). $$ If the edge exists, the one-edge chain makes $F(\Gamma,\Gamma')<+\infty$, so this inequality has an ordinary real right side under the stated no-sinks hypothesis. [F1, F2, F3, given]

2.1 The network’s no-sinks condition and [A1] match the hypotheses of [F4]; its cost is the same $F$ as in step 1.1 by [F2] and [F3]. Thus [F4] supplies one offset function $B$, common to all types, with additivity, positive-scale extensivity and $B(\Gamma)-B(\Gamma')\le F(\Gamma,\Gamma')$ for every pair. [A1, F2, F3, F4, step 1.1]

3.1 Subtract the bound in step 2.1 from that in step 1.1: $$ [\sigma_{\Gamma'}(y)+B(\Gamma')]-[\sigma_\Gamma(x)+B(\Gamma)]\ge0. $$ By the definition of $S$ in the Statement, this is $S_{\Gamma'}(y)\ge S_\Gamma(x)$. The same $B$ works for every admitted transition, proving the conditional weak entropy principle. [step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra] ∎
## Remarks

The cross-type cost, quotient and no-sinks sandwich carriers belong to the mathematical supplier page and are currently draft and unplaced. This item records their exact conditional use; it does not certify those proofs or the physical network assumptions. The stronger no-gap branch in the research notes is an additional hypothesis and is not part of this theorem.

## Statement

For a fixed-composition closed system coupled to an ideal thermal reservoir at $T_0>0$ and ideal pressure store at $p_0>0$, let $Q$ be heat into the system and let $W_{\mathrm{out}}$ be net energy delivered by the system to an ideal work store whose entropy is constant. Assume the isolated-composite bookkeeping of [A1]–[A3] in Facts & Assumptions. Then for any admitted process between equilibrium endpoints $x_i,x_f$,

$$W_{\mathrm{out}}\le G_{T_0,p_0}(x_i)-G_{T_0,p_0}(x_f),\qquad G_{T_0,p_0}(x):=U(x)+p_0V(x)-T_0S(x).$$

If the endpoint states lie on the $(T,p)=(T_0,p_0)$ natural-variable chart, this is the decrease in the Gibbs potential of [[def-td-legendre-potentials]]. Equality requires zero total entropy production; the theorem does not assert that a protocol realizing equality exists.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Fixed composition, equilibrium endpoints, an admitted closed process, $T_0>0$, $p_0>0$, and the ideal reservoir/work-store model below. Use $W_{\mathrm{out}}>0$ for energy delivered by the system, in joules.

[A1] Ideal thermal reservoir: $S_R(E_R)=S_{R,0}+E_R/T_0$ on its accessed energy interval, and heat $Q$ into the system changes reservoir energy by $\Delta E_R=-Q$.

[A2] Ideal pressure and work stores: the only work on the system is $W_{\mathrm{on}}=-p_0\Delta V-W_{\mathrm{out}}$, where the pressure store has energy change $p_0\Delta V$ and the work store receives $W_{\mathrm{out}}$. Both stores have constant entropy; no other work coordinate is admitted.

[A3] The system, bath, and stores form an isolated compound; their only entropy change is $\Delta S_{\mathrm{tot}}=\Delta S+\Delta S_R$, and all omitted kinetic and field-energy endpoint changes vanish.

[F1] [[post-td-first-law-energy]]: The adopted closed-record balance is $\Delta U=Q+W_{\mathrm{on}}$, with positive $Q$ into and positive $W_{\mathrm{on}}$ on the system.

[F2] [[post-td-macroscopic-second-law]]: The isolated compound's equilibrium endpoint entropy change is nonnegative.

[F3] [[def-td-process-and-protocol]]: $Q$ and $W_{\mathrm{on}}$ are process-record transfers, not state functions; an adiabatic record has $Q=0$.

[F4] [[def-td-si-quantities]]: $U$, $Q$, $W_{\mathrm{out}}$, $pV$, and $G$ have units of joules, with $\mathrm{Pa\,m^3=J}$.

## Proof

1.1 By [F1] and the work-transfer model [A2], $\Delta U=Q-p_0\Delta V-W_{\mathrm{out}}$. By [A1] and [A3], $\Delta S_{\mathrm{tot}}=\Delta S-Q/T_0$; [F2] gives $Q\le T_0\Delta S$. The signs of $Q$ and work transfers are those in [F3]. [given, A1, A2, A3, F1, F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 Rearranging the energy balance in step 1.1 gives $W_{\mathrm{out}}=Q-\Delta U-p_0\Delta V\le T_0\Delta S-\Delta U-p_0\Delta V=-\Delta G_{T_0,p_0}$. By [F4], all terms in this inequality have units of joules. This is the stated endpoint bound. [step 1.1, F4, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

The result is a conditional model deduction. A finite reservoir, omitted shaft or field work, matter transfer, or an open-flow energy balance changes [A1]–[A3] and requires a separate argument.

## Statement

Let $X=\mathbb R^4$ and let $\Delta_X=\{(x,y)\in X\times X:x=y\}$.
For $\Psi\in\mathcal D(X\times X)$, define
$$ \langle\delta_{\Delta_X},\Psi\rangle =\int_X\Psi(x,x)\,d^4x. $$
Then $\delta_{\Delta_X}\in\mathcal D'(X\times X)$ is a continuous
complex-linear distribution with support exactly $\Delta_X$, and it is
symmetric under exchanging $x$ and $y$. No nonzero smooth function on
$X\times X$ is supported on $\Delta_X$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The test-function and distribution conventions on Euclidean open
sets.

[F1] $\mathcal D(\Omega)$ consists of smooth compactly supported complex
functions with the LF test-function topology, and $\mathcal D'(\Omega)$ is
its continuous complex-linear dual with bilinear pairing
([[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]], [[def-test-function-topology]],
[[def-distribution]]).

[F2] Smoothness is defined by coordinate derivatives, and composition with a
smooth linear map obeys the total-derivative chain rule
([[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]],
[[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]).

[F3] A continuous function on a compact rectangle is Riemann integrable
([[thm-continuous-on-a-rectangle-is-riemann-integrable]]).

[F4] A compact subset of an open set has a smooth compactly supported cutoff
equal to one near it ([[lem-test-function-cutoffs-and-euclidean-localization]]).

[F5] The support of a distribution is the complement of its largest open
vanishing set ([[def-support-of-a-distribution]]).

## Proof

**Given:** [F1]–[F5].

1.1 Define $d_X:X\to X\times X$ by $d_X(x)=(x,x)$. For $\Psi\in\mathcal D(X\times X)$, the diagonal restriction $x\mapsto\Psi(d_X(x))$ has first derivatives $\partial_{x_j}\Psi(x,x)+\partial_{y_j}\Psi(x,x)$ by [F2]. Iterating this formula on the smooth partial derivatives of $\Psi$ shows the restriction has continuous derivatives of every order, so it is smooth. Its support is contained in the first-coordinate projection of $\operatorname{supp}\Psi$, which is compact as a continuous image of a compact set. Choose a compact rectangle containing that projection; [F3] makes the displayed integral well defined. [F1, F2, F3, construct]

2.1 The assignment is complex-linear. Fix a nonempty compact $K\subseteq X\times X$ and a compact rectangle $R\subseteq X$ containing its first-coordinate projection. For every $\Psi$ supported in $K$, $$ |\langle\delta_{\Delta_X},\Psi\rangle| \le \operatorname{vol}(R)\sup_{(x,y)\in K}|\Psi(x,y)|. $$ Thus the seminorm $q(\Psi)=|\langle\delta_{\Delta_X},\Psi\rangle|$ is continuous on every fixed-support test space. By the LF topology definition in [F1], such seminorms are continuous on $\mathcal D(X\times X)$. Therefore $\delta_{\Delta_X}\in\mathcal D'(X\times X)$. [F1, F3, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 If an open set $U\subseteq X\times X$ is disjoint from $\Delta_X$, then every test supported in $U$ vanishes at every $(x,x)$. Its pairing with $\delta_{\Delta_X}$ is zero, so [F5] gives $\operatorname{supp}\delta_{\Delta_X}\subseteq\Delta_X$. [F5, step 2.1]

4.1 Fix $(x_0,x_0)\in\Delta_X$ and any open neighborhood $U$ of this point. There is a ball $B$ about $x_0$ with $\overline B\times\overline B\subseteq U$. By [F4] choose $h\in\mathcal D(X)$ with $h\ge0$, $h(x_0)=1$, and support in $B$. The product test $\Psi(x,y)=h(x)h(y)$ is supported in $U$, and $\langle\delta_{\Delta_X},\Psi\rangle=\int_X h(x)^2\,d^4x>0$, since continuity makes $h$ positive on a ball about $x_0$. Thus $\delta_{\Delta_X}$ does not vanish on any neighborhood of $(x_0,x_0)$, so $(x_0,x_0)\in\operatorname{supp}\delta_{\Delta_X}$ by [F5]. Since the point was arbitrary, $\Delta_X\subseteq\operatorname{supp}\delta_{\Delta_X}$. Together with step 3.1 this gives equality. [F4, F5, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1]

5.1 For every $\Psi$, the diagonal restrictions of $\Psi(x,y)$ and $\Psi(y,x)$ coincide, so the distribution is symmetric. The diagonal has empty interior: every product neighborhood of a point $(x,x)$ contains $(x,y)$ with $y\ne x$. If a smooth function supported on the diagonal were nonzero at a point, continuity would make it nonzero on an open neighborhood, contradicting empty interior. Therefore every such smooth function is zero. [F2, step 4.1, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

For a nonzero real $g\in\mathcal D(\mathbb R^4)$, the local quartic
functional $L_g(\phi)=\int g(x)\phi(x)^4\,dx$ is not in the regular
polynomial class of [[def-qft-regular-polynomial-functional-algebra]]. Write
$\delta(x-y)$ for the distribution
$\delta_{\Delta_X}$ defined in
[[thm-qft-diagonal-delta-distribution]], and define the diagonal kernel
$K_g$ by
$$ \langle K_g,\Psi\rangle =12\int_{\mathbb R^4}g(x)\Psi(x,x)\,d^4x. $$
The local quartic's second derivative at $\phi\equiv1$ has this kernel.
The verification below shows it is nonzero and cannot be a smooth compact
coefficient kernel, so no other regular presentation can represent $L_g$.
The regular star product in
[[thm-qft-regular-wick-star-associativity]] and the formal time-ordering
construction in [[def-qft-regular-formal-time-ordering]] take regular polynomial
functionals as inputs. Since $L_g$ is not in that class, neither construction
applies to it. Extending either operation across the diagonal requires a
separately stated and proved construction; no such extension or general
causal-renormalization theorem is asserted on this page.

The nonzero hypothesis matters: if $g=0$, then $L_g=0$ is the regular
constant family with all coefficient kernels zero.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** [A1] and [F1]–[F9].

[A1] $g\in\mathcal D(\mathbb R^4)$ is real and nonzero.

[F1] A regular polynomial functional has smooth compactly supported symmetric
coefficient kernels, with the displayed functional derivative kernels
([[def-qft-regular-polynomial-functional-algebra]]).

[F2] Symmetric coefficient representations are unique, and elementary
product tests are dense in the test-function topology
([[lem-qft-tensor-test-function-density]]).

[F3] $\delta(x-y)=\delta_{\Delta_X}$ is a continuous distribution
supported on $\{x=y\}$, pairing with $\Psi$ as
$\int\Psi(x,x)\,d^4x$; no nonzero smooth function is supported on this
diagonal
([[thm-qft-diagonal-delta-distribution]]).

[F4] Tests are smooth compactly supported functions
([[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]).

[F5] A compact set has a smooth compact cutoff equal to one near it
([[lem-test-function-cutoffs-and-euclidean-localization]]).

[F6] The support of a distribution is the complement of its largest open
vanishing set ([[def-support-of-a-distribution]]).

[F7] The LF topology is characterized by seminorms whose restrictions to each

Since $[X_i,X_j](q)=v\partial_z$ for some $v\ne0$ and $b(q)\ne0$, $\omega_q([X_i,X_j](q))=vb(q)\ne0$; hence $\omega_q(Y_t(q))=-tvb(q)+o(t)\ne0$ for all sufficiently small nonzero $t$, so $Y_t(q)$ is transverse to $\ker\omega_q$. Thus $X_1(q),\ldots,X_n(q),Y_t(q)$ are linearly independent. [F2, F3, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 By continuity, choose an open Euclidean ball $B$ about $q$, contained in the coordinate neighborhood, on which $b$ and the vertical coefficient of the same bracket $[X_i,X_j]$ are both nonzero. For each $r\in B$, repeat step 2.1 at $r$ with a sufficiently small nonzero $t=t_r$. The flow of $Y_t$ is $\phi_i^t\circ\phi_j^s\circ\phi_i^{-t}$, a finite horizontal concatenation with both time signs available. Starting at $r$, compose this flow with those of $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ to obtain a $C^2$ endpoint map $\Psi_r$ near the zero duration vector. Then $\Psi_r(0)=r$ and its derivative has the independent columns $X_1(r),\ldots,X_n(r),Y_t(r)$. Choose $|t|$ and the duration neighborhood small enough that every intermediate segment stays inside $B$, using continuity of local flows and that $r$ is interior to $B$. [F1, F2, F3, step 2.1, construct]

4.1 At each $r\in B$, apply [L1] to $H_r(s,p)=\Psi_r(s)-p$ at $(0,r)$, with ambient dimension $2(n+1)$ and target dimension $n+1$, permuting the input to $(p,s)$ so $s$ is solved. Its solved derivative is invertible by step 3.1. Conditionally, some open neighborhood $O_r\subseteq B$ of $r$ consists of endpoints $\Psi_r(s(p))$, all reachable from $r$ by horizontal paths inside $B$. Reachability inside $B$ is an equivalence relation: constant paths give reflexivity, path reversal gives symmetry, and finite concatenation gives transitivity. Every equivalence class is open in $B$, since each of its points $r$ has $O_r$ in that same class. Two distinct classes would separate the connected Euclidean ball $B$ into one nonempty open class and its nonempty open complement, a union of other classes. Thus $B$ is one class: every point of $B$ is reachable from $q$ by a path inside $B$, contradicting (a) with $V=B$. [F1, F3, L1, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 Thus every bracket $[X_i,X_j]$ vanishes by the contradiction at step 4.1. The coordinate identity from step 2.1 gives $d\omega(X_i,X_j)=-\omega([X_i,X_j])=0$, hence $(\omega\wedge d\omega)(\partial_z,X_i,X_j)=0$ for every pair. These evaluations determine the three-form: modulo the $n$-plane $\ker\omega$, the tangent space has dimension one, so every triple reduces by multilinearity and alternation to a multiple of one $\partial_z$ and two horizontal vectors. Therefore $\omega\wedge d\omega=0$. By [F4], condition (b) follows, conditionally on [L1]. [F1, F4, step 2.1, step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 Conversely suppose (b) holds at every point of $U$. The exact global reachability lemma [F8] applies to these local first integrals and the declared horizontal paths. For every $q\in U$ and every open neighborhood $V\subseteq U$ of $q$, it gives a point $p\in V$ not horizontally reachable from $q$ even by a path in $U$, and therefore not by a path in $V$. This proves (a), including neighborhoods larger than an individual first-integral chart, and completes the equivalence. [given, F1, F8] ∎

## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and let $d\ge1$. Let $\phi$ be a stable,
power-tempered pair potential as in
[[def-tdmath-stable-power-tempered-particle-model]], with constants
$B,C,R,\epsilon$ as there. Fix activity $a>0$ and inverse-energy parameter
$\beta>0$ in fixed reference units. Use the free-boundary grand partition sums
$\Xi_L(a,\beta)$ defined in
[[lem-tdmath-particle-exponential-cutoff]]. For $L\ge1$, put
$$p_L(a,\beta):=L^{-d}\log\Xi_L(a,\beta).$$
Then the limit
$$p(a,\beta):=\lim_{L\to\infty}p_L(a,\beta)$$
exists as a finite real number. The assertion is for cubes with free boundary
and the displayed power-tail hypothesis.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, $d\ge1$, a stable power-tempered pair
potential, $a,\beta>0$, and the free-cube partitions in
[[lem-tdmath-particle-exponential-cutoff]].

[F1] [[def-tdmath-stable-power-tempered-particle-model]] defines $U_N$,
stability, and the two-sided power-tail bound.

[F2] [[lem-tdmath-particle-exponential-cutoff]] gives the exact grand
partition definition, $1\le\Xi_L\le e^{QL^d}$, and the particle-cutoff lower
bound, where $Q=ae^{\beta B}$.

[F3] [[lem-tdmath-separated-cube-tail-bound]] gives the uniform bound
$D\le(C/2)Mn^2S_{d,\epsilon}g^{-d-\epsilon}$ on all cross-cube energies.

[F4] [[def-tdmath-measure-integral]] defines the local nonnegative integral as
the supremum over simple minorants; that current batch-11 carrier is a draft
definition with its interface inspected. The local bridge
[[lem-tdmath-measure-integral-agrees-with-root-lebesgue-integral]] proves that
this integral agrees with the shared nonnegative Lebesgue integral. This is the
interface needed to apply the published Tonelli theorem to the partition
integrals.

[F5] [[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]] states that for
sigma-finite measure spaces and a nonnegative product-measurable function, the
product integral equals either iterated integral. The Euclidean product Borel
theorem [[thm-borel-products-of-euclidean-spaces-are-euclidean-borel]] ensures
the finite-configuration integrand is product-measurable.

[F6] [[thm-sigma-finite-product-measure-exists-is-rectangular-and-is-unique]]
supplies the rectangle formula and uniqueness for the finite product measures;
the Lebesgue factors are sigma-finite by
[[prop-lebesgue-measure-is-sigma-finite-and-finite-on-bounded-sets]].

[F7] [[thm-lebesgue-outer-measure-and-measurability-are-translation-invariant]]
preserves each cube integral under a common translation of its particle
coordinates. The corresponding finite product measure is translation-invariant
by the rectangle formula and uniqueness in [F6].

[F8] [[def-countable-choice]] is the exact $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ assumption
used by the Lebesgue-measure suppliers
[[thm-lebesgue-measure-of-a-box-of-every-kind]] and
[[prop-lebesgue-measure-is-sigma-finite-and-finite-on-bounded-sets]]. No full
arbitrary-index choice is used in the block construction.

[F9] Positive real powers obey the exponent laws and are continuous on positive
bases ([[def-real-power]], [[thm-real-power-laws]],
[[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]]). The natural logarithm is
continuous, strictly increasing and onto $\mathbb R$ on $(0,\infty)$
([[def-natural-logarithm]], [[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]]); together with
[[thm-exponential-limits-and-range]], this gives $\ell^\gamma\to0$ for every
$\gamma<0$ and $\ell^\gamma\to\infty$ for every $\gamma>0$.

[F10] [[lem-integer-part]] gives an integer $m$ with $m\le x<m+1$ for every
real $x$.

[F11] Factorials satisfy $0!=1$ and the recursion
$(N+1)!=(N+1)N!$ ([[def-factorial-and-falling-factorial]]).

[A1] Since $p_L$ is defined for $L\ge1$, write
$$\limsup_{L\to\infty}p_L:=\inf_{T\ge1}\sup_{L\ge T}p_L,\qquad \liminf_{L\to\infty}p_L:=\sup_{T\ge1}\inf_{L\ge T}p_L.$$
These are finite because [F2] bounds $p_L$ in $[0,Q]$.

## Proof

1.1 Set $\alpha:=\frac12\bigl(1+d/(d+\epsilon)\bigr)$ and
$g_\ell:=\ell^\alpha$. Then $d/(d+\epsilon)<\alpha<1$ and
$\ell^d g_\ell^{-d-\epsilon}=\ell^{d-\alpha(d+\epsilon)}\to0$ while
$g_\ell/\ell\to0$. Fix a sufficiently large $\ell\ge1$ so that
$g_\ell\ge R$. For $L\ge\ell+g_\ell$, set
$m_L:=\lfloor L/(\ell+g_\ell)\rfloor$. Since $L/(\ell+g_\ell)\ge1$, [F10]
gives $m_L\ge1$ and
$m_L(\ell+g_\ell)\le L<(m_L+1)(\ell+g_\ell)$. Place $M_L=m_L^d$ cubes
$$C_j=(\ell+g_\ell)j+[0,\ell]^d,\qquad j\in\{0,\ldots,m_L-1\}^d.$$
They lie inside $[0,L]^d$ and have pairwise gaps at least $g_\ell$.
[given, F9, F10, construct]

2.1 Fix occupancies $0\le N_j\le n_\ell$ with total $N=\sum_jN_j$. The
ordered configurations in the disjoint cubes with exactly these occupancies
are partitioned by assignments of the $N$ particle labels to cubes. The number
of assignments is $N!/(\prod_jN_j!)$: order all $N$ labels, then note that
each assignment occurs exactly $\prod_jN_j!$ times from within-cube reorderings.
Particle-permutation symmetry of $U_N$ and invariance of the finite product
measure (rectangle formula and uniqueness in [F6]) make the assignment
integrals equal. [F1, F6, F11, given, step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 Restrict the grand partition sum in $[0,L]^d$ to configurations with no
particles outside these cubes and at most $n_\ell$ particles in each cube,
where $n_\ell$ is the cutoff from [F2]. If two cubes have index difference
$k\ne0$, the coordinate gap in a coordinate attaining $\|k\|_\infty$ is at
least $\|k\|_\infty g_\ell$; [F3] therefore bounds the total absolute
inter-cube energy by
$$D_L\le\frac C2M_Ln_\ell^2S_{d,\epsilon}g_\ell^{-d-\epsilon}.$$
Thus $U_N=\sum_jU_{N_j}^{(j)}+U_{\mathrm{cross}}$ with
$U_{\mathrm{cross}}\le D_L$, and
$e^{-\beta U_N}\ge e^{-\beta D_L}\prod_j e^{-\beta U_{N_j}^{(j)}}$;
this remains true when an internal energy is $+\infty$, since both sides then
vanish. [F1, F2, F3, given, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 On each assignment domain from step 2.1, the pointwise lower bound in
step 2.2 factors into nonnegative within-cube integrands. Repeated application
of [F5] and the rectangle formula in [F6] factors their integral into the
product of the translated one-cube integrals; [F7] identifies each with its
origin-centered value. Multiplying by $a^N/N!$ cancels the label count from
step 2.1, leaving $e^{-\beta D_L}\prod_j Z_{\ell,N_j}$. Summing over the
finitely many occupancy vectors and expanding the finite product of cutoff
sums from [F2] gives
$$\Xi_L\ge e^{-\beta D_L}(\Xi_\ell^{\mathrm{cut}})^{M_L}.$$
[F2, F4, F5, F6, F7, F8, step 2.1, step 2.2, algebra]

4.1 The integer-part bounds in step 1.1 give
$L/(\ell+g_\ell)-1<m_L\le L/(\ell+g_\ell)$, so
$m_L/L\to(\ell+g_\ell)^{-1}$ and $M_L/L^d\to(\ell+g_\ell)^{-d}$.
By [F2], $\Xi_\ell^{\mathrm{cut}}\ge(1-e^{-\ell^d})\Xi_\ell$, so
$\log\Xi_\ell^{\mathrm{cut}}\ge\ell^dp_\ell+\log(1-e^{-\ell^d})$.
Taking logarithms in step 3.1, dividing by $L^d$, and using step 2.2 gives
$$p_L\ge\frac{M_L}{L^d}\left(\ell^dp_\ell+\log(1-e^{-\ell^d})-\frac{\beta C}{2}n_\ell^2S_{d,\epsilon}g_\ell^{-d-\epsilon}\right).$$
Taking the lower limit and using the volume ratio above yields the same bound
with $M_L/L^d$ replaced by $(\ell+g_\ell)^{-d}$. The cutoff definition [F2]
and $\ell\ge1$ give
$n_\ell\le K\ell^d+1\le(K+1)\ell^d$. Factoring
$(\ell/(\ell+g_\ell))^d$ and using this estimate in the negative error term
therefore gives
$$\liminf_{L\to\infty}p_L\ge\left(\frac{\ell}{\ell+g_\ell}\right)^d\left[p_\ell+\ell^{-d}\log(1-e^{-\ell^d})-\frac{\beta C}{2}(K+1)^2S_{d,\epsilon}\ell^dg_\ell^{-d-\epsilon}\right].$$
[A1, F2, F9, step 1.1, step 2.2, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 As $\ell\to\infty$, the prefactor tends to $1$. Also
$e^{-\ell^d}\to0$, so continuity of $\log$ at $1$ gives
$\log(1-e^{-\ell^d})\to0$; since $\ell^{-d}\to0$, their product
$\ell^{-d}\log(1-e^{-\ell^d})$ tends to zero. The cross-energy error tends to
zero because $d-\alpha(d+\epsilon)<0$ by step 1.1. The replacement of the
prefactor times $p_\ell$ by $p_\ell$ has error at most
$Q\bigl[1-(\ell/(\ell+g_\ell))^d\bigr]\to0$ by [F2]. Thus for every
$\eta>0$ there is $T$ such that every $\ell\ge T$ makes the right side of
step 4.1 at least $p_\ell-\eta$. [F2, F9, step 1.1, step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 Let $\overline p=\limsup_{\ell\to\infty}p_\ell$. By [A1], for every
$\eta>0$ and every $T\ge1$ there is an $\ell\ge T$ with
$p_\ell>\overline p-\eta$; otherwise the tail supremum from $T$ onward would
be at most $\overline p-\eta$, contradicting the infimum defining
$\overline p$. Choose $T$ large enough for step 5.1. Then
$\liminf_{L\to\infty}p_L\ge\overline p-2\eta$. Letting $\eta\downarrow0$
shows $\liminf p_L\ge\limsup p_L$. [A1, step 5.1, choose, algebra]

7.1 For any $S,T\ge1$, choose $L\ge\max(S,T)$. Then
$\inf_{x\ge S}p_x\le p_L\le\sup_{x\ge T}p_x$. Taking the supremum over $S$
and then the infimum over $T$ proves
$\liminf p_L\le\limsup p_L$ by [A1]. Together with step 6.1, the two finite
tail bounds equal a number $p$. For every $\eta>0$, their definitions give
tail thresholds with $\inf_{L\ge T_-}p_L>p-\eta$ and
$\sup_{L\ge T_+}p_L<p+\eta$; hence $|p_L-p|<\eta$ for all sufficiently large
$L$. The limit is finite by [F2]. This proves existence for the specified
free-cube reduced grand pressure. [A1, F2, step 6.1, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

The proof uses fixed free-boundary cubes. It does not establish a canonical
fixed-density limit, arbitrary-boundary independence, or the corresponding
result for every decreasing integrable tail. In particular, stability alone
does not enter as a claim about arbitrary van Hove shapes; those are separate
interfaces with additional hypotheses. The displayed pressure is per reference
volume and is the reduced pressure (the classical pressure multiplied by
$\beta$). If $L$ is measured in units of a reference length $\ell_0$ and
$\beta$ is the numerical inverse temperature in units $E_0^{-1}$, then the
physical pressure is $P=E_0p/(\beta\ell_0^d)$. Without that specified
classical interpretation, this theorem asserts only the mathematical
existence of the reduced limit.
